chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about a man who has a bondwoman and says, “Whenever I approach her, she is free,” then he sells her to another man and later buys her back. He said: “There is no harm in approaching her; she has gone out of his ownership.”

key_terms.الْأَمَةُ: a bondwoman or female slave owned by a man
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal objection or harm
key_terms.يَبِيعُهَا: he sells her to another person

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man says his bondwoman will be free when he approaches her, then sells and later repurchases her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a conditional emancipation tied to ownership and intercourse. The Imam عليه السلام states that after the bondwoman left the man’s ownership through sale, the prior condition no longer prevented him from approaching her when he bought her again.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3442 - Al-Ala' narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about a man who owned a bondwoman and said: "Whenever I approach her, she will be free." Then he sold her to another man and later bought her back.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in approaching her, as she had exited his ownership."
